These guides are for readers who want to learn `plant` by running small,
complete examples. If you are new to the package, work through **Getting
started** in order, then move on to patches, strategies, and environmental
drivers. For the ideas behind the model, read the
[theory](../theory/index.qmd). For function arguments and return values, use the
[reference site](https://traitecoevo.github.io/plant/reference/).

## Getting started

- [Installation](install.qmd) — install `plant` and check that it loads.
- [Your first individual](first-individual.qmd) — grow a single plant and read
  its state, rates, and trajectory.

After these two pages, continue to [Patch dynamics](patch-dynamics.qmd). A
patch is the smallest simulation in which plants compete with one another.

## Running the model

- [Patch dynamics](patch-dynamics.qmd) — grow a patch of competing plants and
  explore the light environment.
- [Strategies & traits](strategies.qmd) — change parameters, build trait
  matrices, and set control accuracy.
- [Extrinsic drivers](extrinsic-drivers.qmd) — drive a run with time-varying
  rainfall or birth rates.
- [Calibration](calibration.qmd) — understand what calibration requires and
  where it sits in the wider `plant` workflow.

## Worked examples

- [Example analysis](example-analysis.qmd) — the full pipeline, setup to
  results.
- [Self-thinning](self-thinning.qmd) — recover the classic size–density line.
- [Emergent properties](emergent-properties.qmd) — integrate patch outputs up
  to the metapopulation.

## TF24 in depth

- [Hydraulics and acclimation](tf24-hydraulics-and-acclimation.qmd) — compare
  instantaneous optimisation with a gradually acclimating hydraulic state.
- [Non-structural carbohydrate storage](tf24-nsc-storage.qmd) — follow how
  carbon reserves buffer growth and mortality through changing conditions.
